post_title: What cumulative total of locally acquired dengue cases in Florida in 2026 will the FDOH Week 42 Arbovirus Surveillance Report show?

question.title: What cumulative total of locally acquired dengue cases in Florida in 2026 will the FDOH Week 42 Arbovirus Surveillance Report show?
question.description:
Florida in 2026 is experiencing its largest dengue outbreak in decades, concentrated in Hillsborough County (which also reported one death). Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease; "locally acquired" cases are transmitted by Florida mosquitoes rather than imported by travelers. The Florida Department of Health (FDOH) publishes a Weekly Arbovirus Surveillance Report, typically each Thursday, with a year-to-date cumulative count in its "2026 Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida" section.

The cumulative locally acquired dengue total has climbed steeply through 2026: 41 (Week 33, late Aug), 111 (Week 35), 190 (Week 37), 252 (Week 38, published ~Oct 1), 296 (week ending Oct 3, published ~Oct 9), and 368 (Week 40, Oct 4–10, published Oct 15). Recent weekly additions have been large and variable — roughly +38, +62, +44, and +72 in consecutive recent weeks. The report published on or around October 29, 2026 would cover Week 42 (week ending October 24, 2026), reflecting roughly two additional weeks of case accrual beyond the 368 figure. Most cases are in Hillsborough County (310 of 368 as of the Week 40 report), with smaller numbers in Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas, and Polk counties.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative number of 2026 locally acquired ("Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida") dengue cases reported in the Florida Department of Health (FDOH) Weekly Arbovirus Surveillance Report for Week 42 of 2026 (the week ending October 24, 2026), expected to be published on or around October 29, 2026 at https://www.floridahealth.gov/statistics-data/population-surveillance/arbovirus-surveillance/ (direct PDF expected at https://www.floridahealth.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/fl-arbovirus-report-w42-2026.pdf). The resolving figure is the single year-to-date total stated in the "2026 Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida" section (e.g., the report stating "In 2026, 368 cases of locally acquired dengue have been reported" resolves as 368). If the Week 42 report is not available, the most recent Weekly Arbovirus Surveillance Report published on or before October 30, 2026 (and dated after the Week 40 report) will be used instead.
question.fine_print: Only the year-to-date cumulative count of locally acquired (in-state mosquito-transmitted) dengue cases counts; international travel-associated dengue cases are excluded. If FDOH revises the cumulative total in the resolving report relative to prior weeks, the figure printed in the resolving report governs. If no qualifying report is published anywhere by October 30, 2026 and the figure cannot be determined from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), the question is annulled.
